newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices end mixed, heat off, crude steady.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices end mixed, heat off, crude steady.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices ended mixed Monday as forecasts for mild weather in the Northeast inspired the most action in an otherwise sleepy day that saw heating oil fall again after Friday's sharp selloff, traders said.

"Heating oil is looking precarious," said Bob MacMinn, a trader and president of MPAS in Toronto, referring to March heating oil's settlement down a sharp 0.88 cent to at 65.28 cents a gallon. "(Heating oil bearishness) has dominated trade for the last month, he added.
Crude oil for March delivery meanwhile settled just where it started the day, unchanged at $24.15 a barrel.

Crude's lack of change underscored the fact that trading volumes were light Monday amid views a so-far mild winter has wedged oil markets squarely in the doldrums between winter heating oil demand and springtime gasoline demand.
But many traders saw incipient signs of a springtime gasoline rally in Monday's price action, with unleaded futures for March delivery settling a slight 0.09 cent higher at 68.35 cents a gallon.
"We're starting to get the same feeling that we had on heating oil last year," said another trader, referring to how views of low inventories on heat prompted a big rally.
